zajjaj:46-46.t: And His saying: ﴿وَإمّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ الَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ﴾ (And whether We show you some of what We promise them): it is said in exegesis that the battle of “Badr” is meant by it. And it was said that Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — informed the Prophet ﷺ that He would take vengeance on some of this community, but did not inform him whether that would be before his death or after it. What the verse indicates is that Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — informed him that if He did not take vengeance on them in the immediate [world], He would take vengeance on them in the deferred [world], because His saying ﴿أوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإلَيْنا مَرْجِعُهم ثُمَّ اللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ عَلى ما يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ (or We take you in death — to Us is their return; then Allah is Witness over what they do) indicates that. And He has made known how the requital for disbelief and acts of disobedience is.

zajjaj:47-47.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولٌ فَإذا جاءَ رَسُولُهم قُضِيَ بَيْنَهم بِالقِسْطِ وهم لا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ (And for every community is a messenger; so when their messenger comes, it will be judged between them in justice, and they will not be wronged): the meaning — and Allah knows best — is that every messenger is a witness over his community as to their faith and their disbelief, as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْناكم أُمَّةً وسَطًا لِتَكُونُوا شُهَداءَ عَلى النّاسِ ويَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ عَلَيْكم شَهِيدًا﴾ (And thus We have made you a middle community, that you may be witnesses over mankind and the Messenger may be a witness over you) [al-Baqara: 143], and as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَقالَ الرَّسُولُ يا رَبِّ إنَّ قَوْمِي اتَّخَذُوا هَذا القُرْآنَ مَهْجُورًا﴾ (And the Messenger will say, “O my Lord, my people have taken this Qur'an as [a thing] abandoned”) [al-Furqān: 30].
It may also be — and Allah knows best — that Allah made known that He does not punish a people except after giving them excuse and warning, i.e. He did not punish them until the messenger came to them, as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَما كُنّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتّى نَبْعَثَ رَسُولا﴾ (And We would never punish until We sent a messenger) [al-Isrāʾ: 15], and as He said: ﴿رُسُلا مُبَشِّرِينَ ومُنْذِرِينَ لِئَلا يَكُونَ لِلنّاسِ عَلى اللَّهِ حُجَّةٌ بَعْدَ الرُّسُلِ﴾ (messengers as bringers of good tidings and warners, so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers) [al-Nisāʾ: 165].

zajjaj:50-50.t:
And His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ إنْ أتاكم عَذابُهُ بَياتًا أوْ نَهارًا﴾ (Say: “Have you considered: if His punishment should come to you by night or by day…”): ”اَلْبَياتُ“ is anything that happens by night, and it is accusative as [an adverb of] time.
And His saying: ﴿ماذا يَسْتَعْجِلُ مِنهُ المُجْرِمُونَ﴾ (what [part] of it would the criminals hasten?): ”ما“ is in the position of the nominative from two angles. One of them is that ”ذا“ has the sense of [الَّذِي]: “What is it that the criminals would hasten of it?!” It may also be that ”ماذا“ is a single noun, and the meaning is: “What thing would the criminals hasten of it?!” And the hāʾ in ”مِنهُ“ refers back to the punishment, accusative, so the meaning would be: “What thing would the criminals hasten from Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He?!” The better view is that the hāʾ refers back to the punishment, because of His saying: ﴿أثُمَّ إذا ما وقَعَ آمَنتُمْ بِهِ﴾ (Then is it that when it has occurred you will believe in it?) [Yūnus: 51].
And His saying: ﴿آلآنَ وقَدْ كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ﴾ (Now? And you were [before] impatient for it!) [Yūnus: 51]: the meaning is “Now do you believe?!” Al-Farrāʾ claimed that ”آلْآنَ“ is only ”أأنْ كَذا وكَذا؟!“ (“Is it that such-and-such…?!”), and that the alif and lām entered by way of quotation (ḥikāya). But what is by way of quotation — such as your saying ”قامَ“ when you name [someone] by it and make it indeclinable on the fatḥa — does not take the alif and lām.
”اَلْآنَ“ according to Sībawayh is indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, as in: “We, from now (مِنَ الآنَ), will come to you,” so it takes fatḥa. [This is] because the alif and lām enter only for a previously known reference (ʿahd), and ”اَلْآنَ“ — you had no prior knowledge of it before this time, so the alif and lām entered to point to the time; the meaning is: “We, from this time, will do.” So since it contains the meaning of ”هَذا“ (this), it had to be uninflected (mawqūf), and it took fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, namely the alif and the lām.
[Translator's note: the sentence «والهاءُ في ”مِنهُ“، يَعُودُ عَلى العَذابِ، نَصْبٌ، فَيَكُونُ المَعْنى: ”أيُّ شَيْءٍ يَسْتَعْجِلُ المُجْرِمُونَ مِنَ اللَّهِ“» appears corrupt: the paraphrase given (“from Allah”) implies that the hāʾ refers to Allah, and the following sentence prefers its referring to the punishment. It is translated as written.]

zajjaj:53-53.t: And His saying: ﴿وَيَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ أحَقٌّ هو قُلْ إي ورَبِّي إنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ﴾ (And they ask you to inform them, “Is it true?” Say: “Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true”): the meaning [of إي] is “yes, by my Lord.” ﴿وَما أنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ﴾ (and you will not cause failure), i.e. you are not among those who could escape being requited for their disbelief.

zajjaj:54-54.t: ﴿وَأسَرُّوا النَّدامَةَ لَمّا رَأوُا العَذابَ﴾ (And they will conceal remorse when they see the punishment): these are the summoners, the leaders, the disbelievers; they concealed their remorse.

zajjaj:57-57.t: And His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ قَدْ جاءَتْكم مَوْعِظَةٌ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ (O mankind, there has come to you an admonition from your Lord): He means the Qur'an.

zajjaj:58-58.t: And His saying: ﴿قُلْ بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ وبِرَحْمَتِهِ فَبِذَلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُوا﴾ (Say: “In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy — in that let them rejoice”): the lām [of command] originally has kasra. ”فَبِذَلِكَ“ is a badal (substitute) for His saying ”بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ وبِرَحْمَتِهِ“, and it indicates that He means by it the Qur'an as well.

zajjaj:59-59.t: And His saying: ﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ ما أنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ لَكم مِن رِزْقٍ فَجَعَلْتُمْ مِنهُ حَرامًا وحَلالا﴾ (Say: “Have you seen what Allah has sent down to you of provision, and you have made of it lawful and unlawful?”): ”ما“ is in the position of the accusative by ”أنْزَلَ“. The meaning is: “You have made the baḥīra and sāʾiba [camels] unlawful, while Allah did not make that unlawful.”

zajjaj:61-61.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَما تَكُونُ في شَأْنٍ وما تَتْلُو مِنهُ مِن قُرْآنٍ ولا تَعْمَلُونَ مِن عَمَلٍ إلا كُنّا عَلَيْكم شُهُودًا﴾ (And you are not [engaged] in any matter, nor do you recite any of the Qur'an from it, nor do you do any deed, except that We are witnesses over you), i.e. at whatever time you are engaged in some matter of the worship of Allah, and whatever you recite in that matter of the Qur'an. ﴿إذْ تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ﴾ (when you are involved in it), i.e. when you spread out in it; one says ”أفاضَ القَوْمُ في الحَدِيثِ“ when the people spread out in talk and plunged into it. ﴿وَما يَعْزُبُ عَنْ رَبِّكَ مِن مِثْقالِ ذَرَّةٍ﴾ (And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight): it is read ”يَعْزُبُ“ and ”يَعْزِبُ“, with ḍamma on the zāy and with kasra; its meaning is “is not remote.” ”اَلْمِثْقالُ“ and ”اَلثِّقْلُ“ have one meaning. ﴿وَلا أصْغَرَ مِن ذَلِكَ ولا أكْبَرَ﴾ (nor what is smaller than that or greater).
The fatḥa is on [the sense] “Not absent from your Lord is any atom's weight, nor the weight of what is smaller than that, nor greater”; the position is a position of the genitive, but it took fatḥa because it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf). Whoever reads the nominative, the meaning is: “Not absent from your Lord is an atom's weight, nor what is smaller than that, nor greater, except [that it is] in a clear Book,” and the khabar (predicate) is His saying: ﴿إلا في كِتابٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ (except in a clear Book).

zajjaj:64-64.t:
And His saying: ﴿لَهُمُ البُشْرى في الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وفي الآخِرَةِ﴾ (For them are glad tidings in the worldly life and in the Hereafter): it has come in most of the exegesis that ”اَلْبُشْرى“ is the righteous dream which the believer sees in his sleep, and ”وَفِي الآخِرَةِ“ [refers to] Paradise. It is — and Allah knows best — that the glad tidings are what Allah has given them glad tidings of, namely His saying: ﴿يُبَشِّرُهم رَبُّهم بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنهُ ورِضْوانٍ وجَنّاتٍ لَهم فِيها نَعِيمٌ مُقِيمٌ﴾ (Their Lord gives them glad tidings of mercy from Him and good pleasure, and gardens in which there is for them lasting bliss) [al-Tawba: 21]; and this is indicated by: ﴿لا تَبْدِيلَ لِكَلِماتِ اللَّهِ﴾ (There is no changing the words of Allah).
And His saying: ﴿وَلا يَحْزُنْكَ قَوْلُهم إنَّ العِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ (And let not their speech grieve you; indeed honour belongs to Allah entirely) [Yūnus: 65], i.e. let not their threats, their denial and their banding together against you grieve you. ﴿إنَّ العِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ﴾ (indeed honour belongs to Allah) [Yūnus: 65]: indeed dominance belongs to Allah, so He is your helper and the helper of His religion.

zajjaj:66-66.t: ﴿ألا إنَّ لِلَّهِ مَن في السَّماواتِ ومَن في الأرْضِ﴾ (Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth): He does with them what He wills.

zajjaj:68-68.t: And His saying: ﴿إنْ عِنْدَكم مِن سُلْطانٍ بِهَذا﴾ (You have no authority for this): the meaning is: you have no proof for this.

zajjaj:69-69.t:
﴿قُلْ إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلى اللَّهِ الكَذِبَ لا يُفْلِحُونَ﴾ (Say: “Indeed, those who invent a lie about Allah will not succeed”): this is a complete stop (waqf al-tamām).
And His saying: ﴿مَتاعٌ في الدُّنْيا﴾ ([It is but] a brief enjoyment in this world) [Yūnus: 70] is nominative in the sense of “that is a brief enjoyment in this world.” If it were accusative it would be permissible, but it is not read so, because it would contradict the muṣḥaf.

zajjaj:71-71.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَأجْمِعُوا أمْرَكم وشُرَكاءَكُمْ﴾ (So resolve upon your plan and [call] your partners): it is also read ”فاجْمَعُوا أمْرَكم وشُرَكاءَكُمْ“. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that its meaning is “resolve upon your plan and call your partners.” This is a mistake, because the speech [so construed] has no point: if they were calling their partners in order to resolve upon their plan, then the meaning is “resolve upon your plan together with your partners,” as you say: “If the she-camel and her young were left, he would suckle from her,” meaning “if she were left with her young, he would suckle from her.”
Whoever reads ”وَشُرَكاؤُكُمْ“ (nominative) may conjoin it to the wāw [of the pronoun], because the accusative [object] has strengthened the speech. If you said: ”لَوْ تُرِكْتَ اليَوْمَ وزَيْدٌ لَعَلِمْتَ“ (If you were left today, and Zayd, you would know), it would be permissible; but if you said ”لَوْ تُرِكْتَ وزَيْدٌ“, it would be ugly, because you do not conjoin to a nominative pronoun until you strengthen the nominative with a word together with it.
Whoever reads ”وَشُرَكاءَكُمْ“ together with ”فاجْمَعُوا أمْرَكُمْ“ with the connecting alif (waṣl), its accusative is of two kinds. One of them is conjunction onto ”الأمْر“; the meaning is: “resolve upon your plan and gather your partners.” And it may be: “resolve, together with your partners, upon your plan.” ﴿ثُمَّ لا يَكُنْ أمْرُكم عَلَيْكم غُمَّةً﴾ (then let not your plan be obscure to you), i.e. let your plan be open and uncovered, as Ruʾba said:
؎بَلْ لَوْ شَهِدْتَ النّاسَ إذْ تُكُمُّوا بِغُمَّةٍ لَوْ لَمْ تُفَرَّجْ غُمُّوا
(Nay, had you witnessed the people when they were enveloped in a gloom which, had it not been lifted, would have overwhelmed them.)
[i.e.] they were overwhelmed with what is hateful, ”بِغُمَّةٍ“, i.e. with what covers them. Its derivation is from ”اَلْغَمامَةُ“ (the cloud), which covers. ”ثُمَّ لا يَكُنْ أمْرُكم عَلَيْكم غَمَّةً“ is also permissible, i.e. a grief.
﴿ثُمَّ اقْضُوا إلَيَّ ولا تُنْظِرُونِ﴾ (then carry it out upon me and do not give me respite): it has been read ”ثُمَّ أفْضُوا إلَيَّ“. Whoever says ”ثُمَّ اقْضُوا إلَيَّ“, the meaning is “then do what you want”; and ”ثُمَّ أفْضُوا“, with fāʾ, is close in meaning to it.

zajjaj:77-77.t: And His saying: ﴿قالَ مُوسى أتَقُولُونَ لِلْحَقِّ لَمّا جاءَكم أسِحْرٌ هَذا﴾ (Moses said, “Do you say [thus] about the truth when it has come to you? Is this magic?”): this speech is a making [them] acknowledge their saying: ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَهُمُ الحَقُّ مِن عِنْدِنا قالُوا إنَّ هَذا لَسِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ (So when the truth came to them from Us, they said, “Indeed this is manifest magic”) [Yūnus: 76]. ﴿قالَ مُوسى أتَقُولُونَ لِلْحَقِّ لَمّا جاءَكُمْ﴾ (Moses said, “Do you say about the truth when it has come to you…”) this utterance, i.e. “Indeed this is manifest magic”? Then he made them acknowledge, saying: ﴿أسِحْرٌ هَذا ولا يُفْلِحُ السّاحِرُونَ﴾ (Is this magic? But magicians will not succeed). ”اَلْمُفْلِحُ“ is one who attains what he wants, i.e. how can this be magic when the one who brought it has succeeded?! i.e. he has won and prevailed in his argument.

zajjaj:78-78.t:
﴿قالُوا أجِئْتَنا لِتَلْفِتَنا عَمّا وجَدْنا عَلَيْهِ آباءَنا﴾ (They said, “Have you come to us to turn us away from that upon which we found our fathers?”), i.e. to turn us away and divert us. One says ”لَفَتُّهُ عَنِ الأمْرِ، ألْفِتُهُ، لَفْتًا“ when I have diverted him from it; and from this is their saying ”اِلْتَفَتَ إلَيْهِ“, i.e. he turned his face towards him. ﴿وَتَكُونَ لَكُما الكِبْرِياءُ في الأرْضِ﴾ (and that you two may have grandeur in the land): ”اَلْكِبْرِياءُ“ is sovereignty; sovereignty was only called ”كِبْرِياءَ“ because it is the greatest (أكْبَرُ) thing sought in the affairs of this world.
And His saying: ﴿ما جِئْتُمْ بِهِ السِّحْرُ﴾ (What you have brought is magic) [Yūnus: 81], i.e. “Moses said: That which you have brought is magic.” It is also read ”ما جِئْتُمْ بِهِ آلسِّحْرُ“, and the meaning is: “What thing have you brought — is it magic?!” It is by way of rebuke to them.

zajjaj:83-83.t: ﴿فَما آمَنَ لِمُوسى إلا ذُرِّيَّةٌ مِن قَوْمِهِ﴾ (But none believed in Moses except [some] offspring among his people): it was said that he remained calling the fathers, but they did not believe, and a party of their children believed. ﴿عَلى خَوْفٍ مِن فِرْعَوْنَ ومَلَئِهِمْ أنْ يَفْتِنَهُمْ﴾ (for fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs, lest he persecute them): it is permissible to say ”مَلَئِهِمْ“ (their chiefs, plural pronoun) because Pharaoh is one who has companions who take his orders. ”اَلْمَلَأُ مِنَ القَوْمِ“ are the leaders whose word is referred to.

zajjaj:85-85.t: And His saying: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تَجْعَلْنا فِتْنَةً لِلْقَوْمِ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ (Our Lord, make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people), i.e. “Do not destroy us and punish us, so that the family of Pharaoh would think that we were only punished because we are in error.”

zajjaj:87-87.t: And His saying: ﴿واجْعَلُوا بُيُوتَكم قِبْلَةً﴾ (and make your houses a qibla): it has come in exegesis: make your prayer towards the Sacred House. And it was said: ”اِجْعَلُوا بُيُوتَكم قِبْلَةً“, i.e. pray in your houses, so that you may be safe from fear, because they believed in fear of Pharaoh.

zajjaj:88-88.t:
And His saying: ﴿رَبَّنا لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِكَ﴾ (Our Lord, that they may lead [people] astray from Your way): it is also read ”لِيَضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِكَ“ (that they may stray from Your way), i.e. You gave Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world, and that brought them to error, as He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿فالتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهم عَدُوًّا وحَزَنًا﴾ (And the family of Pharaoh picked him up that he might become to them an enemy and a grief) [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8], i.e. “they picked him up, and his affair ended in his becoming an enemy and a grief to them,” not that they intended that he should be an enemy and a grief to them. ﴿رَبَّنا اطْمِسْ عَلى أمْوالِهِمْ﴾ (Our Lord, obliterate their wealth).
It has come in exegesis: i.e. turn their sugar into stones. The interpretation of obliterating (taṭmīs) a thing is removing it from its form and from being benefited from in the first state it was in. ﴿واشْدُدْ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ (and harden their hearts), i.e. seal their hearts. ﴿فَلا يُؤْمِنُوا حَتّى يَرَوُا العَذابَ الألِيمَ﴾ (so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment) is also a supplication against them.
And what Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said is also possible — and Allah knows best. He mentioned that His saying ﴿فَلا يُؤْمِنُوا﴾ is conjoined to His saying ﴿لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِكَ﴾, i.e. “Our Lord, You gave them [this] so that they would go astray and so not believe.”

zajjaj:89-89.t:
And His saying: ﴿قالَ قَدْ أُجِيبَتْ دَعْوَتُكُما﴾ (He said, “Your supplication has been answered”): it is related in exegesis that Moses supplicated and Aaron said “Āmīn” to his supplication. In the verse there is evidence that they both supplicated, because His saying ﴿قَدْ أُجِيبَتْ دَعْوَتُكُما﴾ indicates that the supplication was from them both. The one who says “Āmīn” to the supplication of the supplicant is also a supplicant, because the interpretation of his saying “Āmīn” is “answer [it],” so he is asking as the supplicant asks.
And His saying: ﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعانِّ سَبِيلَ الَّذِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ (and do not follow the way of those who do not know): the position of ”تَتَّبِعانِّ“ is jussive (jazm), but the heavy nūn [of emphasis] entered for the prohibition, emphasizing it, and it was given kasra because it is quiescent and the nūn before it is quiescent. Kasra was chosen for it because it comes after the alif, so it was likened to the nūn of the dual.
﴿وَجاوَزْنا بِبَنِي إسْرائِيلَ البَحْرَ﴾ (And We took the Children of Israel across the sea) [Yūnus: 90]: Allah made it dry land until they crossed it.
